source.author: stat
source.text: subit ille minantem iam tenuis visu, iam vanescentibus armis, iam pedes: exstincto tamen indecerptus in ore augurii perdurat honos, obscuraque fronti vitta manet, ramumque tenet morientis olivae.
source.text_original: ' subit ille minantem / iam tenuis visu, iam vanescentibus armis, / iam pedes: exstincto tamen indecerptus in ore / augurii perdurat honos, obscuraque fronti / vitta manet, ramumque tenet morientis olivae.
source.text_english: He advances against him, now slim in appearance, now with his weapons fading away, now on foot: yet, though extinguished, the honor of the omen remains whole in his face, and a dark fillet remains on his brow, and he holds a branch of the dying olive.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus:
reuse.text_original: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus / extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque / talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus: /
reuse.text_english: and now Cretheus had lifted his faint face to the song, and, looking with sorrow upon both son and daughter-in-law, was opening his lips to say such things, with his blood already poured out:
